item.title: French school riots deepen as experts point to far-left alliance fueling ‘broader confrontation’
item.description: French student protests over school conditions spiral into violent unrest, as experts warn a red-green alliance is fueling a broader revolt,
item.content:encoded:
An unholy alliance is being blamed for instigating the violence seen across France as experts point to a bond between extreme left and radical Islamic groups.

What began as protests over school conditions and funding is entering its third week, and the factors behind the widespread, more violent protests are being debated.

"The protests started in an apparently spontaneous way in the disadvantaged, immigrant suburbs of Paris," Nathalie Szerman, researcher in radicalization and extremism in France at MEMRI, told Fox News Digital, but "it quickly became clear that the violence demonstrated in these protests conveyed a huge amount of hate towards the ‘system’ and not much concern for better material conditions in schools, as dozens of schools across France have suffered vandalism and blockades, and many were even set on fire."

FRANCE ROCKED BY STUDENT RIOTS AS HUNDREDS ARRESTED, VIOLENCE SPREADS NATIONWIDE

Szerman said that while demonstrations over school conditions at the beginning of an academic year in France "is not a new phenomenon," the "scope of these demonstrations and their character should raise concerns." She points to protestors taking to the streets carrying Palestinian flags. "Pro-Palestinian organizations, such as Urgence Palestine, have declared the month of October to be a month of revolt, and these groups are supporting and fueling these demonstrations."

"The French are notorious for strikes, labor shortages and street demonstrations," former U.S. Assistant Attorney General Theo Wold told Fox News Digital, and added that these protests are "a consequence of mass immigration. The rioters are not of French culture, and they don’t respect the rule of law … France is learning that importing an underclass of foreigners causes broader societal damage."

ISRAELI AMBASSADOR COMPARES FRANCE'S FAR-LEFT LEADER'S RHETORIC TO HITLER AS ANTISEMITISM SURGES

Nile Gardiner, director of The Heritage Foundation's Margaret Thatcher Center for Freedom, told Fox News’ Outnumbered on Tuesday, "I think at the very heart of this, is the far-left and the Islamists combining forces to undermine France itself … This is a form of uprising, frankly, by far left wing forces together with second, third generation migrants. And also, at the same time, France is in real economic trouble."

Simone Rodan-Benzaquen, senior envoy to Europe at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital that, "Students have reason to be angry about overcrowded classrooms and absent teachers." She added: "What does Gaza have to do with a shortage of teachers in France? I’ll tell you what: [the far-left La France Insoumise party] has spent years making hostility to Israel a central part of its appeal to young voters. Bringing that cause into the school protests helps fuel the racial dynamics and turn a demand for better classrooms into a much broader confrontation with the government," she said.

EUROPE’S LEFT COURTS MUSLIM VOTERS AS ANTI-ISRAEL POLITICS RESHAPE CONTINENT

"LFI is the perfect embodiment of the Red-Green alliance – the alliance between leftists and Islamists," added Szerman. "LFI rallies Islamist and pro-Palestinian groups on the one hand, and other French anti-system leftists who accuse the elite of enriching itself at the expense of the poor on the other. It is a revolutionary party using Islam as an inner drive. Politicized Muslims are aware of this and are also using LFI to promote their own agenda.

"They are fueling and empowering each other, the common ground being the claim that they are the people," Szerman continued. "The people are seen as the enemy of the ‘elite’ running the country, which therefore has to be overthrown."

Rodan-Benzaquen said, "French students need their teachers to show up to class, and their parents need to know they will be safe at school. But [LFI leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon] is not interested in these goals." She says he is "encouraging the citizens to see their schools as a front in a larger political battle, one whose real prize is the presidency."

FRANCE’S TEEN RIOTS TAKE EXPLOSIVE NEW TURN AS GOVERNMENT POINTS FINGER AT HARD LEFT

French President Emmanuel Macron is term-limited and cannot run for a third consecutive term in elections this coming spring. Many observers believe a runoff match-up between the far-left Mélenchon and right-wing populist Marine Le Pen of the National Rally party could be on the horizon.

"No matter how the protests play out, Mélenchon will likely benefit," said Rodan-Benzaquen. "If the unrest drives voters toward the far right, he can hope to emerge as the leader of the opposition. If he succeeds in mobilizing enough voters himself, he could reach the presidency. Either prospect gives him a reason to keep the confrontation going. Neither gives him much incentive to lower the temperature."

"I do not think that the LFI leadership made a conscious decision to trigger destructive demonstrations all over France," added Szerman, "but once the movement was launched, LFI did provide a backbone for the violence, as it will never blame any of its followers."

FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION

So far, the protests have not spread across the continent even as spending on education seems close between countries.

According to the latest available figures from Eurostat, the European Union’s official statistical office, in 2024 France spent over 5% of its GDP on education, more than it spent on defense. In that same year, neighboring Germany spent only 4.5% of its GDP on education.

In Macron’s latest proposed budget, about $74 billion is earmarked for French schools, more than proposed for defense, but both are cuts from the last official budget narrowly approved by Parliament over the winter. Germany’s Federal Statistical Office reports spending on education was up to 7% of GDP at over $340 billion when including federal, state and local government spending. Meanwhile, in the U.K., Department for Education spending for the 2025/26 school year was estimated at around $142 billion.

When comparing the latest figures for expenditures per student, France’s ministry of education says in the 2024/25 school year, it spent $9,950 per student, Germany’s Federal Statistical Office says $12,000 was spent per student in 2025, and the U.K. spent about $10,100 per student in 2024/25. Meanwhile, the Organization for European Economic Co-operation says the Europe-wide average is around $12,000 per student per year.

Some 500 high schools are closed in France on Wednesday, down from 891 on Tuesday. The schools have been ordered by the ministry of education to replace normal lessons through Friday with structured dialogue and staff crisis management meetings in an effort to calm tensions, to avoid confrontations at school gates and to give staff time to reorganize.

The Associated Press reports more than 6,100 people have been arrested since the protests began, with the Interior Ministry saying 715 police officers have been injured.

Talarico expressed his conditional opposition to males in girls' sports in a September Fox News interview.

"I oppose trans athletes playing in girls’ sports if it endangers safety or fairness," he said.

VULNERABLE DEMOCRATS FLIP ON WOMEN'S SPORTS VOTE AFTER OPPOSING SIMILAR BILLS AS MIDTERMS LOOM

But in 2021, Talarico opposed House Bill 25, which required public-school athletes in interscholastic competition to compete according to the sex recorded on their birth certificates at or near birth, with limited exceptions. Earlier that year, he voted against a bill with a similar purpose, SB 29.

Talarico authored an unsuccessful amendment removing the HB 25's requirement that birth-certificate sex entries be made at or near birth, except for clerical corrections. Before HB 25, the University Interscholastic League accepted legally modified birth certificates reflecting gender identity.

Other amendments he supported would have allowed a coach, principal or school board to approve otherwise prohibited transgender participation. Those provisions did not specify the safety or fairness tests officials would have to apply.

His opposition to laws protecting female athletes from male competitors extended to college sports.

In 2023, he voted against Senate Bill 15, which would have banned biological males from competing on women's college sports teams in Texas. He also supported an unsuccessful amendment allowing transgender athletes to compete under NCAA or NAIA eligibility requirements, with those organizations’ previous rules allowing males to compete in women's sports.

Those organizations have since changed their rules. The NCAA now bars male athletes from women’s competition, while the NAIA reserves its female sports category for athletes whose biological sex is female.

Speaking at the Texas Tribune Festival in September, Talarico rejected any suggestion that his core stance on the issue had shifted.

"No, my position is exactly the same," he stated, reiterating his view that sports eligibility decisions should be made locally on an athlete-by-athlete and sport-by-sport basis, rather than through blanket state bans.

When pressed to explain a controversial 2021 comment where he asserted that "some things are more important than perfectly fair competition in sports," Talarico claimed his original remark had been taken out of context. He explained that he was specifically talking about elementary school recreation and T-ball.

In January, he told "The Ezra Klein Show" that local officials should weigh eligibility and acknowledged that participation would sometimes be prohibited.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

OutKick asked Talarico’s campaign whether he would vote for the federal Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, which would prohibit male participation in female-designated athletics at federally funded institutions and define sex through reproductive biology and genetics at birth.

The campaign’s response did not answer that question, identify a federal alternative or say whether Talarico would vote differently on HB 25 today.

In a follow-up inquiry, OutKick asked how Talarico would measure safety and fairness, including the effects of male puberty, physical advantages, injury risks and lost roster spots or scholarships. The inquiry also asked whether his criteria would vary by age or sport and what binding safeguards he would require under local decision-making.

OutKick also sought an explanation for his amendment removing HB 25’s birth-certificate timing requirement and asked whether he still supports eligibility based on legally amended certificates. It also asked whether he still favors the NCAA/NAIA approach he backed for college sports.

His campaign has not responded to those questions, aside from providing the original statement.

Talarico’s position on the issue returned to the spotlight after Dallas Cowboys legend Randy White challenged his consistency while endorsing Paxton in an exclusive OutKick interview published Oct. 4.

When asked about Talarico’s past votes and recent statements on trans issues, White questioned his motives.

"I think that’s a sign that we can’t trust him," White said. "He’s going to go with the way the wind flows, whatever he feels like is the best thing for him and what his goals are."

item.title: Boxing legend Mike Tyson talks going to juvie and trading cigarettes for cookies as a young boy
item.description: Mike Tyson revealed the wild logistics of transporting his pet tiger across the country, including needing an 18-wheeler from Vegas to New York.
item.content:encoded:
Boxing titan Mike Tyson swung by Jesse Watters' show Tuesday night to chop it up about his past, covering everything from managing exotic cats to growing up in Brooklyn.

First up was the tiger. When you have Tyson on the couch, the famous tiger era is bound to come up. As Tyson tells it, keeping a massive tiger was a real grind.

"A lot of responsibility," Tyson on "Jesse Watters Primetime."

MIKE TYSON CLAIMS HE CAUGHT BRAD PITT WITH HIS EX-WIFE IN WILD THEO VON INTERVIEW

He explained that building a bond with a big cat requires showing up every single day without fail.

"So the name of the game, normally, you have to be with a tiger for two years every day. Can't skip a day or nothing," he said. And if you think traveling with a pet is tricky, try moving a tiger across state lines.

Tyson broke down what it actually took to move his pet around.

"So when I had to travel across the country, I had to get an 18-wheel van to take my cat. So if I'm in Vegas and I gotta go to New York, I gotta get an 18-wheeler for that cat to be driven to New York from Vegas."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

From there, the conversation shifted back to his childhood in Brooklyn. Long before he was fighting in packed arenas, people on his block realized he could throw hands.

"Well, listen, my friends saw me in some fights and they saw me hit some guys who were bigger than me, and I knocked out some of them," Tyson said.

His neighborhood friends saw an opportunity and quickly put young Tyson to work on the street.

SYLVESTER STALLONE SHOWERED IN HIS CLOTHES TO SURVIVE BEFORE ‘ROCKY’ FAME

"So they said I was gonna be the punch guy to knock the guys out, and they were gonna go in the guy's pockets. And that's what they had me do," he recalled.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

That work landed him in juvenile detention as a kid.

Looking back, Tyson didn't offer any heavy life lessons about his time behind bars. Instead, he joked that his main takeaway was "that I could keep coming back and eat some good food."

"When I went there, listen, I went to juvie, and when I first got there, they gave me two cookies, a milk, and two cigarettes. I'm 12 years old," Tyson said.

When asked if he ended up smoking those cigarettes, Tyson showed he had his priorities sorted out early on.

"No, I traded them for cookies."

Just your average stories from a guy who has seen a little bit of everything.

item.title: Ravens players ride with President Trump in motorcade, get shoutout during speech at Baltimore shipyard event
item.description: Marlon Humphrey posted viral video from Trump's presidential motorcade after the Ravens players attended the Anduril Industries shipyard event.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump spent some time with a handful of Baltimore Ravens players on Tuesday during his event at Tradepoint Atlantic, where he touted the site for Anduril Industries' $3.7 billion "Arsenal-2" high-tech shipyard to manufacture submarine components.

During his remarks on the billion-dollar project at the 3,300-acre multimodal industrial and global logistics center located at Sparrows Point in Baltimore County, Maryland, Trump singled out four Ravens players in the audience on their day off.

Four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Marlon Humphrey, kicker Tyler Loop, long snapper Nick Moore and punter Ryan Eckley put on suits to attend the event and met with Trump.

TRUMP TURNS TO EMERGING TECH GIANT IN MULTI-BILLION BID TO RAMP UP US SUBMARINE PRODUCTION

And the president, who is probably the most sports-minded man to ever serve in the Oval Office, pointed them all out and gave the Ravens a shoutout.

"What a team you have this year," Trump said. "What a great team."

The Ravens have a 3-1 record and lead the AFC North division.

Trump met all the players prior to his remarks and then singled them out in front of the assembled audience and media.

"Could you stand up?" Trump asked the players. "You guys are where are you? Big stars. Where are you guys? There they are. Good looking guys."

For some reason, Trump paid particular attention to Moore who is the oldest of the group but perhaps the least recognized player on the team unless he does something wrong when he long snaps on punts and kicks.

"I said, tell me, are you a coach? They said, 'No, he's a snapper,'" Trump said. "You know, nowadays, those long snappers are very valuable. It's an amazing job you do with that. And he's got an unblemished record.

"How far is that, like, 10 yards deep or more? Fifteen yards and you throw strikes, you throw strikes. I don't know how to hell you do it. So, he's got a little gray hair right now, this, but you know, they don't care. They want them him for one play."

JON GRUDEN FIRES UP TRUMP RALLY CROWD IN OHIO AS IF DELIVERING A LOCKER ROOM SPEECH THEN DELIVERS ENDORSEMENT

As part of the event at least a couple of the players got a bit of a surprise in that they joined Trump in the tour of the facility in the presidential motorcade.

Humphrey sat directly behind Trump and shot a video of the president and Moore talking about a past Super Bowl.

He posted the video on X and within hours the post had one million views.

And, of course, some folks loved it. And some folks didn't.

A lot of the discussion in the comments revolved around – surprise! – racism.

Here are some of the comments: nope, on second thought, not worth the energy of typing them. One can be certain, however, that this meeting will be a topic of conversation in the Ravens locker room when players return to work on Wednesday.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson, the team's biggest star, was not present at Tuesday's event. He is nursing an ankle injury and his status for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons is uncertain.

But Jackson was on the president's mind.

"Say hello to your quarterback," Trump told the other players. "He’s a little bit injured. And tell him I know his mother. I met his mother a few times in Palm Beach. And she’s a fantastic, beautiful woman. Give him my regards. He is some player."

item.title: Bar named in Cornell rape lawsuit disputes accuser's account, says she was never served alcohol while underage
item.description: An Ithaca, New York, bar disputed the Cornell University gang-rape accuser's claim it served her alcohol underage on the night of the alleged Chi Phi assault.
item.content:encoded:
A bar named in the lawsuit at the center of the Cornell University sexual assault firestorm is disputing the alleged victim's claim that it served her alcohol while she was underage on the night of the alleged assault — a denial the bar has now also lodged in court.

Moonies Bar & Nightclub, a downtown Ithaca, New York, bar popular with Cornell students, told Fox News that underage guests at a private Tri Delta sorority event on Oct. 19, 2024, were marked on their hands, while guests over 21 received wristbands. The bar says its bartenders served alcohol only to guests wearing wristbands.

The complaint and Moonies' account both say Doe was marked as underage. They differ over whether she was then served alcohol.

Doe's lawsuit alleges a Moonies bouncer placed an "X" on each of the then-20-year-old's hands to signify she was under 21, but that she was nevertheless served and consumed at least one alcoholic beverage inside the bar.

INSIDE EXPLOSIVE CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS: 7 MEN ACCUSED, CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS AND A POLITICAL FIRESTORM

"No alcohol was served to anyone who had mark on their hands," Moonies said in a statement to Fox News Tuesday, disputing the allegations.

CORNELL PRESIDENT SAYS UNIVERSITY 'MUST DO BETTER' ON HANDLING OF SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS

Moonies also told Fox News that Doe later worked for the company from February to March 2025 and discussed the October 2024 incident during that period.

According to the bar, Doe never said during those conversations that she had been intoxicated at Moonies or served alcohol by one of its bartenders.

Fox News Digital contacted Doe's attorney for a response to both of Moonies' assertions.

In a formal answer filed Sunday in New York Supreme Court, Zareen Enterprises LLC, which does business as Moonies Bar & Nightclub, denied unlawfully selling or furnishing alcohol to anyone under the legal drinking age and denied selling or furnishing alcohol to any visibly intoxicated person.

The filing specifically denies the paragraph of Doe's complaint alleging she was served alcohol at Moonies despite having been marked as underage. Moonies also denied that any act or omission on its part caused Doe's alleged injuries.

The bar asked the court to dismiss the complaint against it in its entirety.

The dispute comes as the case has roiled Cornell and drawn national attention, with thousands rallying on campus Monday and faculty senators now pushing a no-confidence resolution against the university's central administration over its handling of sexual assault. Gov. Kathy Hochul has also appointed the New York Attorney General's Office as special prosecutor, with Attorney General Letitia James leading an "active criminal investigation."

Moonies said it hosted the private Tri Delta event from 9 p.m. to 11 p.m. that night with about 185 guests, including roughly 150 who were over 21 and 35 who were underage.

The bar said it had a contract with the sorority and marked underage guests' hands while providing wristbands to those over 21.

In the statement, Moonies called Doe's allegation that she was served alcohol "completely inaccurate," saying its employees "strictly followed the rules and did not serve alcohol to any underaged guests."

WATCH: CORNELL STUDENTS PROTEST SCHOOL'S HANDLING OF SEXUAL ASSAULT INVESTIGATION:

CORNELL PICKS FORMER DEPUTY US ATTORNEY GENERAL TO REVIEW SEX ASSAULT RESPONSE

In its court filing, Moonies also asserted as affirmative defenses that Doe cannot establish that it unlawfully sold alcohol to an underage or visibly intoxicated person, or that any alleged unlawful sale caused her injuries. The bar maintained that it complied with all applicable laws and regulations governing alcohol sales.

The dispute concerns one part of Doe's account of the hours preceding the alleged assault and what happened at Moonies before she arrived at Chi Phi.

According to her lawsuit, Doe began the evening drinking vodka at her Tri Delta sorority house before a sorority housemother accompanied her to Moonies. She later went to another Ithaca bar before leaving alone around 11 p.m. and walking to the Chi Phi fraternity house to meet a friend who was a member.

By the time she arrived at Chi Phi, Doe was visibly intoxicated and had consumed roughly 10 standard drinks over three hours, according to her complaint.

Once inside, Doe alleges she was given another beer before going upstairs, where two fraternity members pressured her into snorting what they said was ketamine, a drug she says she had never previously taken. She alleges they also gave her marijuana and high-proof liquor before sexual activity began.

Doe alleges other fraternity members became involved as the night progressed and that she eventually became "completely incapacitated." Seven former Chi Phi fraternity brothers are accused in her lawsuit of sexual assault and rape.

The men have denied wrongdoing, with some maintaining that sexual activity was consensual and others denying they participated. No criminal charges have been filed against the seven men.

The case burst into public view when Doe filed the 101-page lawsuit Sept. 16, nearly two years after the alleged encounter.

In addition to the seven former fraternity members, Doe sued Cornell University, Chi Phi and affiliated entities, her own Tri Delta sorority and Moonies, among others, alleging that institutions around her failed to protect her before, during and after the events of that night.

The lawsuit's allegations prompted renewed scrutiny of the original criminal investigation.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who initially declined to pursue charges, has said the six-page sworn statement his office received from Cornell University Police in 2024 did not allege that Doe was drugged against her will or gang-raped and instead described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as "voluntary, conscious, and consensual."

A fuller transcript of Doe's November 2024 police interviews later obtained by CBS New York included statements in which she distinguished the initial sexual encounter from later activity and explicitly told investigators she had been raped.

Van Houten said his office had never received that transcript.

Fox News' Michelle Langer contributed to this report.
